chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
He has disbelieved in Allah, the one who disavows from a lineage, and even if it was lowly.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on disowning one's lineage in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this concise yet profound statement from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), linking the denial of one's biological lineage directly to a fundamental breach of faith. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on 'nasab' not merely as social identity but as a divine trust, where disowning even a humble ancestor is viewed as rejecting the natural order established by Allah. It serves as a counter to tribal arrogance, affirming that all Muslims share a common human origin and that kinship ties (silat al-rahim) are a core component of religious observance.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abu Baseer, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘He has disbelieved in Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, the one who disavows from a lineage, and even if it was lowly’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from abu Basir from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) has said, ‘
It is to disbelieve Allah to disown one’s lineage even though it (the lineage) is very lowly.’”
